newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers take to Brussels streets.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers take to Brussels streets.

text.p: Thousands of chanting workers from Renault Belgium, with steelworkers giving their support, marched through Brussels on Monday to protest plans by the French company to close their factory.

Chanting "Renault Stays Open" and throwing firecrackers, workers passed riot police surrounding the main European Union institutions without incident, although windows of some nearby buildings were smashed.
"C4. Merci Louis," read one placard, referring to the form Belgians must complete to claim unemployment benefit and Renault boss Louis Schweitzer.

The demonstration was swelled by workers from the Belgian unit of Caterpillar, which is also facing restructuring and Belgian radio reported that some 2,300 workers from bankrupt Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq would also join later.

Renault said last Thursday it would close its plant in Vilvoorde near Brussels with the loss of 3,100 jobs as part of a reorganisation of production designed to save it 825 million French francs ($140 million) a year.
In France, the newspaper Les Echos reported that Renault is expected to announce plans to cut about 3,000 jobs in France on top of the Belgian closure.
Vilvoorde's production of Megane and Clio models would be moved in July to existing factories in France and Spain, the company said.
The Belgian government condemned the decision as brutal and unacceptable but Schweitzer has said there is no chance the company will change its mind.
The Belgian workers want French and Spanish colleagues to stage supportive protests following meetings scheduled to take place later on Monday.
Bond traders said the markets were watching events closely for any political fallout.
"The government has enough problems as it is. This is just one more it could have done without," one trader said.
